claims.value: Bodart’s footnote gives 37,000 Austrians against 30,000 French fighting on 21 May, and 85,000 against 50,000 on 22 May.
claims.rationale: Day-specific engaged subsets distinct from the table’s 99,000/66,000 available totals; the two days are not summed. English rendering (ours): "On 21 May 37,000 Austrians fought 30,000 French; on 22 May 85,000 fought 50,000."

claims.value: Pelet transmits an Austrian report of 103 battalions, 148 squadrons and 75,000 men, 288 guns, then expressly disputes its adequacy.
claims.rationale: Mediated opponent report within Pelet’s family, not a separately inspected return. His preferred 90,000–100,000 French estimate is an alternative, not an adjudication. English rendering (ours): "According to the Austrian report their army comprised 103 battalions, 148 squadrons, which they reduce to 75,000 men, with 288 guns."

claims.rationale: Masséna as Duke of Rivoli and Bessières as Duke of Istria appear in the same inspected paragraph. English rendering (ours): "The right, consisting of the second army corps under Marshal Lannes, rested on Essling."

claims.value: Pelet contrasts Lannes’s belief in a 6,000–8,000 rear guard with Masséna’s belief that the whole Austrian army was nearby.
claims.rationale: Beliefs reported retrospectively; not actual Austrian strength. Masséna’s opposing belief is on the same inspected page. English rendering (ours): "The impetuous Lannes claimed there was before us only a rear guard of six to eight thousand men."

claims.rationale: Interested defence of Napoleon; retained as a source dispute, not substituted for the frozen outcome. English rendering (ours): "This action, at most indecisive."
